A fault with the signalling system in the Honor Oak Park area means that some lines will be blocked. As a result of this, trains running between Sydenham and New Cross Gate may be cancelled, delayed or revised.
Disruption is expected until 14:00.
Customer advice:
The fault with the signalling system is affecting trains operating through the Sydenham Corridor between East Croydon and New Cross Gate. As a result, some services are unable to operate, whilst others are being diverted away from the affected route.
Passengers travelling between London Bridge, New Cross Gate, Norwood Junction, East Croydon, Gatwick Airport and destinations further south should expect delays, cancellations and extended journey times. You should allow an additional 45 minutes extra to complete your journey today.

• Thameslink Services between Bedford and East Grinstead
• Southern Services between Norwood Junction and London Bridge
• Southern Services between London Bridge and London Victoria
• Southern Services between Epsom and London Bridge
Great Northern services that normally run between Cambridge and London Kings Cross will now call additionally at Ashwell & Morden until further notice. Customers travelling to or from Ashwell & Morden should use these amended services and allow additional time for their journeys.

Passengers should use available Thameslink services between Three Bridges and Bedford which are being diverted via Herne Hill. Southern services to London Victoria can be used with onward connections via London Underground on any reasonable route.

Can you tell me more about the incident?
Track circuits are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. If one fails, the signalling system may show that a section of track is occupied even when there isn’t a train there. This means signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and request verbal permission from the signaller before continuing past the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely should they see anything ahead of them.
This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.
